episodes.title: Morning Truck Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the lot and walk to your light truck. You check gas, oil, water, tires, lights, and brakes. Everything looks ready for the day.

trial.title: Order your check
items: Drive out of the lot
Check tires, lights, and brakes
Check gas, oil, and water
Walk around the truck and look it over
trial.explain: You look the truck over first, then check equipment and supplies before driving.

episodes.title: Checking Todays Load
episodes.text: You open the back doors and pick up the shipping papers. You count the boxes and match them to the list. You close the doors once it matches.

episodes.title: Same Roads Again
episodes.text: You drive the route and stop at red lights. You signal and stay in your lane. You do the same stops you did yesterday.

episodes.title: Lost On Route
episodes.text: You pull over and call in for help finding the next stop.

choice.prompt: You missed the turn on the verbal directions. What do you do?

options.label: Pull over and ask them to repeat it
options.outcome: You stay parked and write it down. You get back on the route on the next try.

options.label: Keep driving and guess the way
options.outcome: You miss more turns. You have to stop and call again.

chat.text: Where are you right now?
Stay there, take the next right, then second left.

episodes.title: Brake Feels Wrong
episodes.text: You press the brake and it feels soft under your foot. You pull over safely and stop the truck. You need to report the problem.

choice.prompt: The brake feels soft. What do you do next?

options.label: Report it now and stay parked
options.outcome: You call it in and wait for instructions. The truck stays parked until it is cleared.

options.label: Keep driving to finish the route
options.outcome: You risk losing braking on the road. You break traffic safety rules.

episodes.title: Last Map Stop
episodes.text: You sit in the cab and read the map for the last drop. You follow the written directions street by street. You pull up to the address on the paper.

episodes.title: Morning Trays Ready
episodes.text: You arrive and start in the sterilization room. You run the instruments through and lay out clean trays for the day. You set out materials so each room is ready.

trial.title: Get a room ready
items: Seat the patient and place the bib
Mix and set out the filling materials
Run instruments through the sterilizer
Lay out the clean instrument tray
trial.explain: You sterilize first, then set the tray and materials before the patient sits down.

episodes.title: First X-Rays
episodes.text: You bring in your first patient and explain the x-rays. You place the sensor and step out to expose the images. You check that they came out clear for the dentist.

choice.prompt: The first image comes out blurry because the patient moved. What do you do?

options.label: Reposition and retake it
options.outcome: You settle the patient again and retake the image. The second set comes out clear.

options.label: Keep the blurry image
options.outcome: You save the blurry image. The dentist cannot read it and asks you to bring the patient back.

episodes.title: Chairside With Dentist
episodes.text: You sit down chairside as the dentist starts a filling. You pass instruments and hold suction as asked. You keep the area clear and watch the patient.

episodes.title: Counting Supply Boxes
episodes.text: You sit in the storage room with the clipboard. You count boxes and check what is low. Same list as yesterday, same check tomorrow.

episodes.title: Patient Feels Faint
episodes.text: A patient goes pale in the chair and says they feel faint.

choice.prompt: The patient is slumping and dizzy in the chair. What do you do first?

options.label: Recline the chair and stay with them
options.outcome: You recline the chair and stay close, reporting to the dentist. The team takes over emergency care together.

options.label: Leave to get supplies
options.outcome: You step away to the storage room. The patient is left alone until the dentist calls you back.

options.label: Sit them upright with water
options.outcome: You try to sit them up for water. They feel dizzier and the dentist asks you to recline them instead.

chat.text: Stay with them, recline the chair back.
Tell me their pulse if you can feel it.
I feel dizzy, everything is spinning.

episodes.title: Writing Day's Notes
episodes.text: You sit at the desk with the charts open. You record what treatment was done for each patient today. You double-check names and close the records.

episodes.title: Morning Charts
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with today's folder. You open the first chart and review the medical history. You note allergies and changes before you call anyone back.

episodes.title: First Look
episodes.text: You greet your first patient and settle them back in the chair. You feel along the gums and look closely for sores and redness. They shift a little when you touch a tender spot.

choice.prompt: The patient winces when you touch a sore area. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and ask about the sore
options.outcome: You stop for a moment and ask when it started. You write it down with the rest of the history.

options.label: Keep the exam moving gently
options.outcome: You ease your touch and finish looking at the rest of the gums. You come back to the sore spot at the end.

episodes.title: Measuring Gums
episodes.text: You pick up the probe and check around each tooth. You watch for recessed areas and signs of gum disease. You call out what you see for the record.

trial.title: What needs attention
trial.scenario: You are probing the gums and checking for disease. One back section looks recessed and bleeds easily. The rest looks pink and firm.
options: The recessed section that bleeds
The pink firm sections
Recheck the medical history form
trial.explain: You note the recessed and bleeding area first because it shows signs of disease.

episodes.title: Another Cleaning
episodes.text: You clean deposits and stains from the teeth and just under the gum margins. It is the same motions as yesterday. It will be the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sore You Find
episodes.text: Your afternoon patient is in the chair and you start the gum check.

choice.prompt: You see a raw sore with swelling beside it. What do you do now?

options.label: Stop the cleaning and flag it
options.outcome: You set your instruments down and record the sore carefully. You tell the patient it needs the dentist to look today.

options.label: Clean lightly around it
options.outcome: You work carefully around the sore without pressing on it. You record what you saw for follow-up.

options.label: Finish the full cleaning first
options.outcome: You finish the planned cleaning and add the sore to your notes. You ask the front desk to have the dentist check it.

chat.text: That spot on the side has hurt for a week.
It bleeds when I brush. Is that bad?

episodes.title: Brushing Lesson
episodes.text: You sit up with your last patient and talk through brushing and flossing. You show them where plaque sits along the gum line. They practice the motion back to you.

episodes.title: Gloves Mask Glasses
episodes.text: You pull on your mask, gloves, and safety glasses before the first patient. You check the fit and toss the gloves between rooms. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Checkup Begins
episodes.text: You sit down and lean the chair back. You look at teeth and gums with your mirror and probe. You pull up the x-rays to check what you cannot see.

episodes.title: Talking Through Treatment
episodes.text: You sit beside the patient with the chart in hand. You walk through what you found in the teeth and gums.

choice.prompt: You have the exam and x-rays. What treatment plan do you lay out now?

options.label: Fill the cavity now
options.outcome: You explain the filling step by step. The patient nods and you book the procedure.

options.label: Watch it and recheck next visit
options.outcome: You explain what to watch for and note it in the plan. The patient leaves with a recheck date.

chat.text: Is it bad?
Do I need work now or can it wait?
What would you do for my teeth?

episodes.title: Filling The Tooth
episodes.text: You pick up the hand instrument and start the dental air turbine. You clean out the decay and place the filling. You check the bite and smooth the edge.

trial.title: Exam in order
items: Diagnose disease or abnormality
Take x-rays for hidden areas
Formulate plan of treatment
Look at teeth and gums with instruments
trial.explain: You look first, then check x-rays, then diagnose, then plan treatment.

episodes.title: Pain Breaks Through
episodes.text: You are halfway through the procedure when the patient lifts a hand. They feel sharp pain where you are working. You pause and keep your instruments still.

choice.prompt: The patient still feels pain. What do you do about the anesthetic?

options.label: Give more anesthetic and wait
options.outcome: You give more anesthetic and wait a few minutes. The area goes numb and you continue.

options.label: Pause and check the numbness first
options.outcome: You stop work and test the area gently. You give a little more anesthetic before you go on.

episodes.title: Writing Treatment Notes
episodes.text: You sit at the desk after the last visit. You write down the treatment plan for the teeth and mouth tissue. You note what to do next time.

episodes.title: Morning Health Checks
episodes.text: You log in from home and open the same system status screens. You check each service against its expected state. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Talking Through Limits
episodes.text: You join a video call with the programmer and systems analyst. You walk through what the project needs and what the current setup can handle.

choice.prompt: The analyst wants a feature that will not fit the time left. How do you handle it?

options.label: Suggest a smaller version that fits the time
options.outcome: You agree on the smaller scope and note the limits for the plan. The team moves on with a clear build target.

options.label: Ask for more detail before you decide
options.outcome: You stay on the call ten more minutes listing needs and constraints. You leave with a list to review against cost and time.

episodes.title: Checking What Users Need
episodes.text: You sit down with the new software requests. You compare what users asked for against time and cost. You mark what is feasible to design now.

episodes.title: Testing the New Build
episodes.text: You pull up the new build at your desk. You write out the test steps and run through them. You note each pass and fail.

trial.title: Order the testing steps
items: Document what you tested and what happened
Run the checks against the new build
Write the test steps for the change
Fix the code where the test fails
trial.explain: You write the steps first, then run them, fix failures, and document the result.

episodes.title: System Out of Spec
episodes.text: You see one service is running outside its expected limits.

choice.prompt: The monitor shows the system is out of spec. What do you do first?

options.label: Keep watching a few more minutes to confirm
options.outcome: You watch the readings and save the logs. You confirm it stays out of spec and flag it to the team.

options.label: Pause the rollout and check the failing part
options.outcome: You hold the install and look at the failing checks. The system stays down until you clear the issue.

options.label: Call the engineer to compare notes
options.outcome: You share your screen and compare readings. You both agree on what is off-spec and what to check next.

chat.text: Seeing the same spike on your side?
Can you confirm if it is still in spec?
It just crossed the limit again.

episodes.title: Writing Install Notes
episodes.text: You open the install document for today's software change. You write down the steps you took and the test results. You save it where the team can find it.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Dialysis Technician — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Lifting the Truck
episodes.text: You arrive in the cold shop and pull on your gloves. You position the hydraulic jack under the front axle. You raise the truck until the wheels hang clear.

episodes.title: Checking the Brakes
episodes.text: You sit on a low stool by the open wheel. You inspect the brake system, steering parts, and wheel bearings. You turn each part by hand to check its condition.

choice.prompt: The brake lining looks thin but still passes. Do you flag it now or leave it?

options.label: Flag it now
options.outcome: You mark it for reline and move it up the repair list. It gets fixed today.

options.label: Leave it for now
options.outcome: You note it in your head and keep inspecting. You will check it again next service.

episodes.title: Tightening More Bolts
episodes.text: You go down the row with your wrench and tighten bolts and screws. Same pattern as yesterday. Same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Relining the Brakes
episodes.text: You pick up your handtools and pneumatic wrench. You adjust and reline the brakes and align the wheels. You reassemble the equipment and torque it down.

trial.title: Put the brake job in order
items: Reassemble the equipment
Reline the brakes
Tighten the bolts and screws
Adjust the brakes
trial.explain: You reline first, then adjust and tighten, then put it all back together.

episodes.title: Losing Brake Pressure
episodes.text: You press the brake pedal and it sinks to the floor. You see fluid at the brake line fitting. You know this truck cannot leave like this.

choice.prompt: The line is leaking and the truck is booked out. What do you do first?

options.label: Keep it on the hoist for repair
options.outcome: You leave it raised and start the brake line repair. The truck stays until it holds pressure.

options.label: Lower it and move it outside
options.outcome: You lower it carefully and push it to the holding spot. You fix it there before it leaves.

episodes.title: Reading the Gauges
episodes.text: You attach the test instruments to the engine. You read the dials and pressure gauges. You write down what looks off for tomorrow.

episodes.text: You start the main work of a Digital Forensics Analyst — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Morning Run Sheet
episodes.text: You arrive before the lot fills up. You sit down with yesterday's notes and today's customer requests. You write out the daily work and run schedule for crews and trucks.

episodes.title: First Trucks Out
episodes.text: You look at the requests and the open crews. You pick which service vehicle goes to which location. You reach for the radio and the phone to send them out.

choice.prompt: Two jobs need a crew at the same time and you have one crew open. What do you do?

options.label: Send the open crew to the waiting customer job
options.outcome: You radio the crew to the customer's address. The other job waits until the next crew frees up.

options.label: Call your supervisor before you assign anyone
options.outcome: You explain both requests on the phone. You assign the crew the way your supervisor tells you.

episodes.title: Watching The Board
episodes.text: You sit by the radio and watch your assigned territory. Nothing new comes in for a while. Same as yesterday, same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Customer Needs Answers
episodes.text: A customer calls with questions about service and equipment.

chat.text: Can you tell us when our truck is coming?
Dispatch, what should I tell them about the equipment?
Check the schedule and give them a straight answer.

episodes.title: Driver Stuck Roadside
episodes.text: A driver calls in with a problem on his run.

choice.prompt: Your driver is stuck and his customer is waiting. What do you decide first?

options.label: Dispatch another service vehicle to the customer
options.outcome: You radio the nearest free crew to that location. The stuck driver waits for help while the customer still gets service.

options.label: Relay the problem to your supervisor first
options.outcome: You call your supervisor and pass along the driver's location and message. You wait for direction before you move other crews.

options.label: Tell the driver to wait and hold all other trucks
options.outcome: You tell the driver to stay put on the radio. The other trucks stay on their runs until you have a plan.

chat.text: Dispatch, I'm stopped on the route. What do you want me to do?
Find out where he is and get cover for that stop.

episodes.title: Passing Every Message
episodes.text: You sit back on the radio and phone. You relay work orders and messages between crews and supervisors. You keep each message short so nothing gets mixed up.

trial.title: Pass the work order
items: You speak the work order to the crew on the two-way radio
You receive the work order from the supervisor
You pick the right crew channel on the radio
You hear the crew repeat the message back
trial.explain: You get the order first, then reach the right crew, then speak it and hear it back.

episodes.title: Morning Hello in Barn
episodes.text: You arrive before the yard wakes up. You stand by the stall door and talk low so the mare hears your voice. You let her sniff your hand and lean into contact.

episodes.title: Teaching Basic Obedience
episodes.text: You bring the young gelding into the round pen for his training session. You work on standing still and walking forward when asked. You repeat the pattern until he holds the behavior.

choice.prompt: He keeps shifting his feet instead of standing. What do you do now?

options.label: Stay and repeat the stand exercise
options.outcome: You stay with him and repeat the stand five more times. He stands a little longer, but the rest of the morning runs late.

options.label: Move on to walking work
options.outcome: You switch to walking work and he follows more easily. You make a note to come back to standing tomorrow.

episodes.title: Circling the Ring Again
episodes.text: You walk the same circle you walked yesterday. You use the same voice and rein cues to keep the pace steady. You do it again, and then again.

episodes.title: Fitting the Harness Work
episodes.text: You lead the mare out for harness training. You check how she moves in the harness at a walk. You adjust your cues to her pace and size.

trial.title: Order the harness steps
items: Cue the horse to pull forward in harness
Let the horse feel the harness weight standing still
Talk to the horse and let it accept touch
Walk the horse with rein cues to steer
trial.explain: You settle the horse with voice and touch before you add weight or ask it to move.

episodes.title: Spook During Show Practice
episodes.text: You are cueing the gelding through a practice show run. He startles halfway through and plants his feet.

choice.prompt: He is tense and refusing your cue to move forward. What do you do?

options.label: Give a calm cue to wait, then recue
options.outcome: You give him a moment, then cue again with a light hand signal. He takes a few stiff steps forward and finishes the pass.

options.label: End the run and walk him out
options.outcome: You stop cueing and walk him calmly out of the ring. He relaxes on the walk, and the practice run is over.

chat.text: He stopped cold at the same spot. Want me to stand by the rail?
Say the word and I will stay quiet or step back.

episodes.title: Last Ride Check
episodes.text: You saddle the quiet mare for rider work. You use voice and rein commands to ask for walk and stop. You finish when she carries and halts smoothly.

options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Demonstration Lesson
episodes.text: You meet your first student beside the car and start with the basics. You demonstrate mirror checks and smooth braking while you talk through each move. The student watches, then tries the same short stretch.

trial.title: Calm reply practice
trial.says: I keep stalling at the junction. I can't do this.
options: You can keep trying. Let's talk through the steps together and try once more.
You are just not cut out for driving.
Forget the mirrors, nobody really uses them anyway.
trial.explain: Encouraging discussion and another careful try matches patient instruction.

episodes.title: Watching How She Drives
episodes.text: You sit beside your next student on a quiet street. You watch her steering and braking to see what she can already do.

choice.prompt: She keeps rushing her mirror checks. What do you do now?

options.label: Talk it through and show it again
options.outcome: You discuss the misses and demonstrate the check again. She practices it slowly on the next street.

options.label: Say nothing and move on
options.outcome: You leave the notes blank and keep driving. She keeps making the same rushed checks.

chat.text: I get so nervous at roundabouts.
I understand better when we just talk it through.
Am I doing okay so far?

episodes.title: Same Circuit Again
episodes.text: You take the midday group around the same practice circuit. You repeat the same points about signals and lane position. It is the same as yesterday, and tomorrow will be the same.

episodes.title: Changing the Lesson Plan
episodes.text: You sit with a student who learns better by talking than by reading. You set aside the handout and switch to discussion with short practice stops. You keep the same driving goal but change how you teach it.

episodes.title: Stalled in Traffic
episodes.text: Your student stalls at a busy junction and cars queue behind you. His hands tighten on the wheel and he wants to quit for the day. You keep your voice steady and keep the car safe.

choice.prompt: He says he wants to stop trying. What do you do?

options.label: Encourage one more calm try
options.outcome: You ask him to breathe, restart, and try the junction once more with you talking him through. He makes it through shakily.

options.label: End the drive there
options.outcome: You swap seats and drive back yourself. The lesson ends early without another try.

options.label: Suggest extra practice later
options.outcome: You agree to pause, then plan another session to work on junctions. He leaves still unsure but willing to return.

episodes.title: Filing Student Records
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk after the last drive. You enter today's lessons and progress notes for each student. You check each file is complete before you close it.

episodes.title: Morning Aircraft Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the pad with the drone on the table. You check the engines, controls, instruments, and other systems before anything leaves the ground.

trial.title: Order your preflight check
items: Check the instruments
Check the engines
Check the other systems
Check the controls
trial.explain: You work front to back in the same order every time.

episodes.title: Calculating Takeoff Speed
episodes.text: You sit down with the flight sheet. You look at airport altitude, outside temperature, aircraft weight, and wind speed and direction. You work out the speed you need to get airborne.

episodes.title: Flying With Co-Pilot
episodes.text: You sit in as co-pilot for the morning leg.

choice.prompt: Your co-pilot asks you to take captain's duties for the landing. Do you take them?

options.label: Take the landing
options.outcome: You take the controls and fly the landing pattern. Your co-pilot watches the systems and calls the heights.

options.label: Stay as co-pilot
options.outcome: You stay on monitors and call out readings. Your co-pilot keeps the controls through landing.

chat.text: I have the climb, you have the monitors?
Call out if fuel or systems look off.

episodes.title: Same Sky Patrol
episodes.text: You fly the same route as yesterday. You watch engine operation, fuel use, and systems. Same checks, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Clouds Close In
episodes.text: The visibility drops and you can no longer see the horizon. You shift your eyes to the instruments to hold course.

choice.prompt: The visibility is poor and the instruments are your only reference. What do you do?

options.label: Fly fully on instruments
options.outcome: You keep your eyes on the instruments and hold steady heading and height. You stay on that until the air clears.

options.label: Hold position and wait
options.outcome: You slow and hold where you are on instruments. You wait for the visibility to improve before moving on.

episodes.title: Watching Fuel Burn
episodes.text: You are back in the air for the last leg. You monitor engine operation, fuel consumption, and the systems page. You log the numbers as they change.

episodes.title: Reading the Plans
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and pull the blueprints from your bag. You sit on a stack of drywall and read through the sheets. You check what goes where and what you will need today.

episodes.title: Marking the Walls
episodes.text: You stretch your tape along the wood framing in the bedroom. You hold your square straight and pencil your marks for the first sheets. The corner number on the wall does not match the blueprint.

choice.prompt: Your mark and the blueprint differ by two inches. What do you do?

options.label: Remeasure from the corner
options.outcome: You hook the tape again and find you started at the wrong edge. You fix the marks.

options.label: Go with the mark on the wall
options.outcome: You keep the wall mark and cut the sheet short. You have to recut it later.

episodes.title: Hanging Board Again
episodes.text: You lift another sheet onto the wood frame. You drive screws in a steady line down the studs. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cutting Outlet Openings
episodes.text: You hold the panel for the living room wall. You measure for the electrical outlets and windows. You cut the openings with your keyhole saw.

trial.title: Cut an outlet opening
items: Cut along the lines with the keyhole saw
Measure where the outlet box sits
Set the panel to check the opening
Mark the outline on the panel
trial.explain: You measure first, then mark, then cut, then check the fit.

episodes.title: Framing the Doorway
episodes.text: You are at the hallway doorway fitting metal trim with your coworker.

chat.text: This trim piece still rocks a little. Hold it tight?
Ready to screw this side when you are.

episodes.title: Vent Hole Missed
episodes.text: You lift the last sheet and see the vent opening sits half off the frame.

choice.prompt: The vent cut does not line up. What do you do now?

options.label: Trim and adjust the opening
options.outcome: You mark the overlap and widen the cut with the saw. The panel drops into place around the vent.

options.label: Cut a fresh panel
options.outcome: You lay out a new sheet and cut the vent opening again. The bad sheet goes in the scrap pile.

episodes.title: Morning Orders Open
episodes.text: You arrive and open your laptop. You sit down and pull up the order software. Overnight orders wait in a short list.

trial.title: Sort the morning orders
items: Create invoices for the confirmed orders
Open the order management software
Set orders to move forward automatically
Check the new overnight orders
trial.explain: You open the list first, then make invoices before anything moves on.

episodes.title: Boxes and Labels
episodes.text: You stand at the packing table with today's sold items. You pack each box and add the shipping paperwork inside. You move finished boxes to the pickup spot for direct shipping.

episodes.title: Shipping Question Call
episodes.text: You see a new message from a customer about shipping. You open it to answer.

choice.prompt: The order is not shipped yet. Do you change the shipping method now?

options.label: Change it and explain the difference
options.outcome: You update the shipping method and tell them the new arrival day. They thank you and keep the order.

options.label: Leave it as ordered
options.outcome: You explain it will ship with the method they picked. They decide whether to keep it or cancel.

chat.text: Hi, will this arrive by Friday? I picked the wrong shipping method.
Can you change it before you send it?

episodes.title: Running Same Payments
episodes.text: You sit back down to run payments. You open the payment screen and process each one the same way. Same clicks as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Declined Payment Problem
episodes.text: You see a payment did not go through. The order cannot move to packing. The customer writes asking why the order is stuck.

choice.prompt: The card was declined. What do you do next?

options.label: Ask them to try another payment
options.outcome: You send clear steps to pay again with the electronic service. The order waits until the new payment clears.

options.label: Cancel the order for now
options.outcome: You stop the order and tell them how to order again later. The invoice stays closed.

options.label: Try running the same card again
options.outcome: You run the same card once more in the payment service. It still declines and you have to message them.

episodes.title: Confirmations Sent Out
episodes.text: You return to your desk for the last block. You check which orders and shipments finished today. You send each customer an email confirming the transaction and shipment.

episodes.title: First Hello
episodes.text: You knock and step into the curtained bay. You pull up a stool next to the bed.

chat.text: Is this going to hurt?
I'm kind of nervous about this test.
Can you tell me what you are going to do?

episodes.title: Morning Heart Tracing
episodes.text: You clean the skin and place the leads for the EKG. You watch the line jump across the screen and the tracing looks noisy. The patient is shifting and breathing fast.

choice.prompt: The tracing is noisy and the patient keeps moving. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and help them settle
options.outcome: You stop the recording. You help them lie still and breathe slow, then you start a clean tracing.

options.label: Keep recording through the noise
options.outcome: You keep the machine running. The tracing stays messy and you will likely have to repeat it.

episodes.title: Same Tracing Again
episodes.text: You set up another EKG. You place the leads, record the activity, and check the strip. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Wall Thickness
episodes.text: You sit at the screen with the echo numbers. You compare the heart wall thickness and chamber sizes to the posted norms. You mark where they line up and where they do not.

trial.title: Spot what is off
trial.scenario: You compare the echo numbers to the standard norms. Three chamber sizes sit inside the normal range. One wall thickness number sits well above the normal range.
options: The high wall thickness
A normal chamber size
The time on the clock
trial.explain: You flag the value that falls outside the standard norms.

episodes.title: Break In Sterile Field
episodes.text: You are standing in the procedure room holding the sterile tray. You see a non-sterile sleeve brush the edge of the field.

choice.prompt: You saw the touch on the sterile field. What do you do right now?

options.label: Speak up and stop the use
options.outcome: You point to the touched spot and step back. The team pauses and replaces the contaminated cover.

options.label: Say nothing and keep going
options.outcome: You stay quiet and hold the tray out. The team keeps using a field that may no longer be sterile.

options.label: Adjust the drape yourself
options.outcome: You reach over the field to fix it. Your move risks another touch and the team still must re-do the setup.

chat.text: Did that just touch the drape?
We need this field sterile. What do you see?

episodes.title: Writing Down Numbers
episodes.text: You watch the ultrasound screen and listen to the signals. You write down the blood pressure, limb volume changes, and oxygen saturation. You check the numbers once more before you file them.

episodes.title: Morning Wash Up
episodes.text: You arrive and hang up your coat. You sit down beside her bed and say good morning. You help her wash her face and brush her teeth.

episodes.title: Walk Down Hall
episodes.text: You help him stand and get steady on his feet. You walk slowly with him down the hall and back. You stay close while he catches his breath.

trial.title: Check What Is Off
trial.scenario: You take his pulse and blood pressure after the short walk. His pulse feels much faster than this morning. His skin looks pale and damp.
options: Wait and recheck his blood pressure later
Report the fast pulse and pale skin first
Offer him water and keep walking
trial.explain: A fast pulse with pale skin after light activity needs attention before anything else.

episodes.title: Showing Daughter How
episodes.text: You sit with his daughter at the bedside to show morning care.

choice.prompt: She holds his arm wrong and looks at you. Do you correct her now?

options.label: Guide her hands now
options.outcome: You move her hands gently and she practices the safe hold twice.

options.label: Let her try alone
options.outcome: She tries once on her own, then you show her the safe hold again.

chat.text: I’m scared I’ll hurt him if I move him.
You show her how to support his arm.
Like this? Do I lift here?

episodes.title: Afternoon Checks Again
episodes.text: You take the blood pressure and pulse again. You check the pill box and note what was taken. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Something Seems Off
episodes.text: You notice she is more confused and unsteady than this morning. You sit with her and check her again. You know you need to tell your supervisor.

choice.prompt: Her condition has changed. What do you do first?

options.label: Call your supervisor now
options.outcome: You call right away, describe the change, and stay with her until you get direction.

options.label: Wait until end of day
options.outcome: You stay with her, keep watching, and the change is still there to report later.

options.label: Ask family to decide
options.outcome: The family worries with you, and you still call your supervisor for direction.

episodes.title: Notes and Team Talk
episodes.text: You sit down and write up the care and progress notes. You record the services and the change you saw today. You join the team review to plan what comes next.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Electrical Engineer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Blueprint Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and set your tool bag down. You open the blueprint on the tailgate and trace the kitchen circuit with your finger. You mark the wall where each box goes so it matches code.

episodes.title: Kitchen Rewire Talk
episodes.text: You stand in the kitchen with your coworker looking at the marked wall.

choice.prompt: The mark for the second box looks a little off from the blueprint. What do you do?

options.label: Recheck the blueprint together
options.outcome: You both look at the print again and fix the mark. You drill and mount on the right spot.

options.label: Go with the first mark
options.outcome: You mount the box where it is marked. You have to move it later to match the print.

chat.text: Blueprint shows two boxes on this wall, right?
Want me to hold it while you mark the second one?
Say where and I'll stay put.

episodes.title: Pulling Wire Again
episodes.text: You pull insulated wire through conduit in the hallway wall. You do the same pull you did yesterday in the next room. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Testing the Circuit
episodes.text: You sit on the floor by the finished run with your test lamp. You touch the leads to the wires in each box. You watch for light to show the circuit is complete.

trial.title: Find the dead box
trial.scenario: You test three boxes on one run. Two boxes light your test lamp. One box stays dark.
options: This box is not connected yet
The blueprint paper is torn
The ladder is too short
trial.explain: If the others on the same run work, this box is the one to check.

episodes.title: Dead Outlet Upstairs
episodes.text: You climb the ladder to check a bedroom outlet that shows no power. You open the box and see a wire has slipped loose. You hold your tester ready to check it again.

choice.prompt: The loose wire is in your hand. What do you do first?

options.label: Turn off the breaker then fix it
options.outcome: You climb down and switch the breaker off. You fix the wire safe and the tester lights up.

options.label: Push the wire back in now
options.outcome: You push the wire back while it is still live. You get a shock and have to stop and turn the breaker off.

options.label: Leave it and test another room
options.outcome: You close the box and climb down. The outlet stays dead until someone fixes it.

episodes.title: Fixtures Going In
episodes.text: You stand at the counter with your hand tools and mount the switches and outlets. You tighten each fixture into its box. You test each one to make sure it works.

episodes.title: Morning Tools Ready
episodes.text: You arrive early and lay out the day's equipment. You sterilize each piece and set it in place. You wipe down the work areas until they are clean.

episodes.title: Same Clean Again
episodes.text: You bring in your client and cleanse the skin with water, cream, and lotion. You work through the same steps as yesterday. It will be the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing Skin Care
episodes.text: You sit down with a client who wants to care for her skin at home. You start to show her how to clean it properly.

choice.prompt: She asks what she should do at home each day.

options.label: Show a simple daily cleanse
options.outcome: You demonstrate water, cream, and lotion step by step. She copies you once and writes it down.

options.label: Suggest a basic care routine
options.outcome: You talk through morning and night care and which products to use. She asks a few questions and thanks you.

chat.text: I just scrub fast in the morning. Is that okay?
Can you show me how you do it?
What should I use at home?

episodes.title: Finding Good Colors
episodes.text: You look closely at your client's skin in the daylight. You hold a few products and colors near her cheek. You pick the ones that suit her skin quality best.

trial.title: Pick the right match
trial.scenario: You hold three product colors near a client's cheek. Two blend softly with her skin. One looks gray and sits heavy on dry patches.
options: Set aside the gray, heavy color
Set aside a blending color
Use all three together
trial.explain: You skip the shade that looks gray and heavy on her skin.

episodes.title: Dirty Tray Before Client
episodes.text: You turn to start and see the tray is not fully clean. Your next client is already seated and waiting. You cannot touch the skin like this.

choice.prompt: Your client is waiting but the equipment is not sterile.

options.label: Stop and sterilize properly now
options.outcome: You explain the short wait and sterilize the equipment and clean the area. You start once everything is clean.

options.label: Quick wipe and keep going
options.outcome: You consider it, then see the tools still need full cleaning. You stop and do the full sterilize instead.

episodes.title: Writing Client Notes
episodes.text: You sit down with your record book at the end of the day. You write down each client's needs and preferences. You list the services you provided today.

episodes.title: Morning Panel Check
episodes.text: You arrive in the machine room and open the control panel. You check the wiring connections and control panel hookups. You check the alignments and clearances of the car and hoistway.

episodes.title: Same Shaft Checks
episodes.text: You walk the same hoistway and check the same door installations and clearances. You write down the same readings you wrote yesterday. You move on knowing you will do it all again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Holding The Doors
episodes.text: You kneel by the open landing with your coworker to set the door installation. You hold the track steady together.

choice.prompt: The door track will not sit straight in the frame. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and realign it now
options.outcome: You loosen it and shift it until it sits straight, then you fix it down solid.

options.label: Fix it down as is
options.outcome: You tighten it crooked and the doors drag, so you have to loosen it and start over.

chat.text: Can you hold this side up while I line up the track?
Does this look straight to you before we fix it down?

episodes.title: Building The Car
episodes.text: You climb into the bare car frame after lunch. You set the platform, lift the walls, and hang the doors. You tighten everything with hand tools.

trial.title: Put the car together
items: Hang the doors
Set the platform in place
Lift and fix the walls
Bring the car frame together
trial.explain: The car has to go together from the frame up before the doors can hang right.

episodes.title: Stuck Door Lock
episodes.text: You get the call that a car is stopped with a door that will not lock. You open the unit and find a worn lock and burnt electric wiring. You shut the power down to disassemble the defective unit.

choice.prompt: You have the unit open with a bad lock and bad wiring. What do you fix first?

options.label: Replace the electric wiring first
options.outcome: You cut out the burnt wiring and replace it, then you test with your meter before touching the lock.

options.label: Replace the lock first
options.outcome: You pull the worn lock and fit the new one, then you turn to the wiring before restoring power.

episodes.title: Signing The Report
episodes.text: You sit at the machine room desk with your service report. You check that safety regulations and building codes are met. You complete the report verifying conformance to standards.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Embedded Systems Engineer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Checking Supply Binders
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the preparedness binders. You check dates, swap an old contact sheet for a new one, and initial the log. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Listening to the School
episodes.text: You sit down with a school principal in a quiet office. You ask what buses, nurses, and accessible rooms they have if a storm hits. You write down what they can do and where they fall short.

trial.title: Asking about needs
trial.says: We have one nurse and two buses — what else do you need to know from us?
options: That is probably enough, we will figure out the rest later.
Can you walk me through where students with medical needs would go and who stays with them?
You should just buy more buses and hire more staff.
trial.explain: You need clear details about needs and capabilities to plan for an emergency.

episodes.title: County Planning Call
episodes.text: You join county staff and a neighboring town liaison around a table. You compare plans and talk through who sends personnel and equipment if help is needed. You agree on who calls whom next time.

choice.prompt: The county wants to change the equipment-sharing list today, but one town has not reviewed it yet. What do you do?

options.label: Wait for their review
options.outcome: You leave the list as is and set a time to revisit it. Everyone keeps using the current plan until then.

options.label: Update it now
options.outcome: You write in the change and send the new list to all liaisons. The missing town gets a call from you to catch up.

episodes.title: Opening the Shelter
episodes.text: A flash flood warning comes in for the low streets. You move to coordinate evacuation and shelter opening with local officials.

choice.prompt: The water is rising and the shelter is not fully staffed yet. What do you order first?

options.label: Order the evacuation now
options.outcome: You call for evacuation of the low streets and open the shelter with current staff. More staff join as residents arrive.

options.label: Wait until fully staffed
options.outcome: You hold the order for twenty minutes while staff travel in. Buses wait and the shelter opens late.

chat.text: Water is up on River Road. Do we need to open the school shelter?
Buses are ready. Special needs van is on standby.

episodes.title: Writing the Status Report
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk after the response. You draft the situation status report on response efforts, current needs, and early damage notes. You keep it short and factual for officials.

episodes.title: Updating Contact Sheets
episodes.text: You pull out the resource materials for the preparedness plans. You update phone numbers, shelter capacity notes, and equipment lists. You file everything so it is ready in the morning.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a EMT / Paramedic — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.

episodes.title: Morning Video Call
episodes.text: You log on and open the intake notes. Your new client joins the video call to go over income and expenses.

choice.prompt: You need more detail on taxable income and deductible expenses. What do you ask for now?

options.label: Ask for delivery pay records and mileage and receipts
options.outcome: You get the missing pay statements and receipts. You can see what counts as income and expenses.

options.label: Move on with only the part-time wages
options.outcome: You start with incomplete numbers. You will have to come back later for the missing delivery details.

chat.text: Hi, I worked part-time and did some delivery driving too.
I am not sure what counts as income or what I can deduct.
Can you tell me what else you need from me?

episodes.title: Simple Return Draft
episodes.text: You open the tax software for an individual client. You enter wages and a few expenses. You start building the simple return line by line.

trial.title: Put the math in order
items: Look up the amount in the tax tables
Add up the income figures on your calculator
Figure out if tax is owed or overpaid
Complete the entries on the form following the instructions
trial.explain: You add first, enter correctly, check the tables, then compute the result.

episodes.title: Entering Numbers Again
episodes.text: You sit with the calculator and the forms. You check figures and type them in again. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Every Deduction
episodes.text: You review a small business return for missed savings. You apply the adjustments, deductions, and credits that fit. You keep the total tax as low as the rules allow.

episodes.title: Numbers Do Not Match
episodes.text: You compute the total and it shows a balance owed. Then you see a missing expense sheet the client just sent. You need to fix the entries before the return goes out.

choice.prompt: The return is almost ready but the new expenses change the total. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and recompute with the new expenses included
options.outcome: You redo the math and entries. The corrected return shows the right amount owed or overpaid.

options.label: File now and fix it later
options.outcome: You keep the old math for now. You will need to amend the return after it is filed.

episodes.title: Sending Clear Instructions
episodes.text: You write a short note to a taxpayer about their form. You explain what to sign and where to enter the last figures. You check that the advice matches the form instructions.

episodes.title: Morning Case Counts
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk with coffee. You open the surveillance system and check last night's infectious disease counts. You log the same numbers you logged yesterday.

episodes.title: Tracing the Source
episodes.text: You pull up charts for a cluster of stomach illness in town. You compare who got sick, where they ate, and when symptoms started. You map how the illness may have spread from person to person.

episodes.title: Teaching Prevention Basics
episodes.text: You stand in a clinic break room with five healthcare workers. You explain how this communicable disease spreads and how to prevent it. One nurse asks about telling patients who are scared.

choice.prompt: The nurse asks what to stress most to worried patients right now.

options.label: Focus on hand washing and staying home when sick
options.outcome: They nod and write it down for their next patients. You stay a few minutes to answer follow-up questions.

options.label: Walk through the full life cycle of the disease
options.outcome: They listen quietly and take notes. You offer a simple handout they can share with patients later.

episodes.title: Filing the Reports
episodes.text: You sit back at your computer after lunch. You fill in the forms for this week's infectious disease incidents. You send the report to the local and state health agencies.

episodes.title: Sudden Spike Alert
episodes.text: You see a sharp jump in new cases on the afternoon update. You call your supervisor to check the numbers together.

choice.prompt: You have to decide what to do about the spike first.

options.label: Report the spike to the state now and keep investigating
options.outcome: You send the early counts and note you are still checking the cause. The state asks for an update tomorrow.

options.label: Investigate for one more day before reporting
options.outcome: You spend the afternoon calling clinics for details. You have a clearer picture to report the next morning.

options.label: Ask your boss to decide the timing
options.outcome: Your boss reviews the numbers with you. You both agree to send a short alert this afternoon.

chat.text: That jump looks real. Are you seeing it too?
Yes. Ten new cases from the same neighborhood.
We may need to alert the state today.

episodes.title: Sharing What You Found
episodes.text: You join a call with local health practitioners and a policy maker. You share what you found about this disease and its risk factors. You answer their questions in plain language.

trial.title: Answering clearly
trial.says: So what should we tell the public about this disease?
options: Share the main findings on risk and prevention in simple words.
Say the research is too complex for the public to understand.
Guess at the cause before the investigation is done.
trial.explain: Your job is to share clear findings about risk and prevention.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Again
episodes.text: You arrive and wipe down the bed, the tray, and the tools. You sterilize what needs it and set out clean linens. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: First Cleanse
episodes.text: You greet your first client and drape her hair back. You wash your hands and cleanse her skin with water and cream. You rinse and pat dry so you can see her skin clearly.

trial.title: Order the cleanse
items: Pat the skin dry to see it clearly
Wash your hands before you touch her face
Cleanse her skin with water and cream
Drape her hair back from her face
trial.explain: You keep hair and dirty hands away first, then you cleanse and finish dry.

episodes.title: Matching Product and Color
episodes.text: You look close at her skin in daylight. You test two lotions and one tint on her jaw. You pick the one that sits smooth and looks like her skin.

episodes.title: Showing Home Care
episodes.text: You hand her the cleanser and show her how much to use.

choice.prompt: She wants to keep scrubbing hard at home. What do you do?

options.label: Show her the gentle wash
options.outcome: You show her soft circles with cream and water. She copies you and feels the difference.

options.label: Let her keep scrubbing
options.outcome: You say nothing and she leaves. Her skin stays red from scrubbing at home.

chat.text: I just scrub hard at home. Is that wrong?
Show her the gentle routine before she leaves.

episodes.title: Shade Looks Wrong
episodes.text: You put the color on and it looks orange on her cheeks. She frowns in the mirror and waits. You need to fix the product choice now.

choice.prompt: The color you picked looks wrong on her skin. What do you do?

options.label: Wipe it off and re-match
options.outcome: You cleanse it off and test a lighter tone. The new shade blends and she relaxes.

options.label: Tell her it will settle
options.outcome: You leave the orange tone on. She pays and does not book again.

options.label: Ask her to pick one herself
options.outcome: She picks a jar at random. It streaks and you both know it is not right.

episodes.title: Writing Notes Down
episodes.text: You sit down with the client cards. You write what skin products you used and what she liked. You file them so tomorrow you remember.
